findings.title: Windows occupancy stdout framing rejects a normal successful zero count
findings.analysis: The helper writes compact JSON plus a text newline using sys.stdout.write. CPython 3.9.13 initializes Windows stdout with newline=None and translates LF to CRLF, including redirected stdout. Parent Popen uses binary PIPEs and accepts only b'{"count":0}\n'. Normal successful output is therefore b'{"count":0}\r\n' and is rejected as PROFILE_OCCUPANCY_UNPROVEN even with count=0 and exit=0. PYTHONIOENCODING affects encoding, not newline translation. The original suite calls open_owned directly and never exercises occupancy.
findings.impact: The exclusive live directory, start intent and worker claim already exist before occupancy. The candidate fails before navigation while consuming the single start. This is a fail-closed framing defect, not platform or actual profile-occupancy evidence.
findings.required_correction: Under separate authority, define consistent binary framing or strictly decode and validate one JSON record with explicitly permitted framing. Keep malformed output, stderr, nonzero exit and nonzero count rejected. This review authorizes no repair, candidate, suite, live run or marker reset.
findings.proof_kind: Frozen code plus version-specific primary CPython source; no product/helper execution.

findings.title: Final viewer decision can ignore an asynchronous guard stop
findings.analysis: The readiness loop checks stopped/failure only before awaited password and viewer reads. A concurrent denied request or callback failure can set terminal guard state during either await; control can then assign LOGIN_REQUIRED or AUTHENTICATED_VIEWER_OBSERVED without rechecking. Policy denial sets stopped but can leave failure=None. The final result does not serialize the pre-shutdown stopped state; finally itself sets stopped for cleanup. A normal exit0 outcome can therefore coexist with an already observed unexpected network stop. On the precheck exception path, original guard.failure is not copied because guard_failure is assigned only after a successful loop.
static_counterexample: Iteration begins with stopped=False and failure=None.
DOM await yields; a live handler denies a request or records an error and sets stopped=True.
DOM await returns the expected viewer/route and password absence.
Current code assigns authenticated outcome without another terminal guard check.
findings.impact: First unexpected failure and original error retention are not authoritative at the final decision boundary. The local suite uses expected_block=True and does not exercise the live decision.
findings.required_correction: Under separate authority, recheck and preserve terminal guard state/first error after asynchronous reads and at serialization; distinguish shutdown-only stopping. No repair or new execution is authorized here.
findings.proof_kind: Static possible interleaving, not an observed platform event.
